post.text: 🚨: High school student, 18, invents water filter that eliminates 95.5% of microplastics https://t.co/vVFxUOZuto

description.description: A close-up macro photograph of a person's fingertip with a small pile of microplastics on it. The particles are very small, granular, and consist of white and scattered blue fragments, highlighting their tiny scale relative to the ridges of the fingerprint.

A head-and-shoulders portrait of a young woman with long light-brown hair, smiling at the camera. She is wearing a light blue and white striped collared shirt and two delicate necklaces. The background is a plain, neutral grey wall.

botInput.comments:
- **@FascinatingTrue** (Likes: 4052): The high school student you are referring to is Mia Heller, an 18-year-old from Warrenton, Virginia. 

Unlike traditional filters that use expensive physical membranes that frequently clog, Heller's system uses ferrofluid—a magnetic liquid.
- **@ChronosIntelX** (Likes: 3136): 🧲 She didn't use a membrane. She used magnets.
Mia Heller, 18, built the system in her garage in 2025. The mechanism: ferrofluid bonds to microplastic particles as water flows through. A magnetic field pulls the entire mixture out. The ferrofluid gets recovered and reused.
Result: 95.52% of microplastics removed. Standard municipal treatment plants remove 70 to 90 percent.
A 2025 University of New Mexico study found microplastic concentrations in human brain tissue rose 50 percent in less than a decade.
She built a better answer in a garage.

Reference :-Smithsonian Magazine March 2026, Regeneron ISEF 2025, University of New Mexico microplastics study 2025
